newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish president asks Yilmaz to form new govt.
newsitem.headline: Turkish president asks Yilmaz to form new govt.

text.p: Turkish secularist Mesut Yilmaz said the president had asked him on Friday to form a new government to replace the coalition of Islamist Prime Minster Necmettin Erbakan.
"A while ago, the president gave me the responsibility to form a new government," Yilmaz told reporters at the presidential palace.
Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist leader, resigned under pressure from the secularist army on Wednesday.
Yilmaz's Motherland Party has only 129 deputies in the 550-seat parliament and may struggle to find enough allies from the squabbling secularist factions to win a confidence vote.

Two leftist parties have pledged their support for Yilmaz but a secularist alliance would still need backing from a small right-wing group and around a dozen defections from Tansu Ciller's True Path Party.
